Recommended controls: freeze preprocessing seed=0, training seed=42, splits, routing, validation users and candidates across all four categories. A common seed alone does not ensure identical shared parameters after adding modules: copy matching tensors from one baseline initialization and verify equality; initialize additions independently. Separate RNG streams for initialization, data ordering, negative sampling, dropout and diagnostics; preserve shared stochastic draws where feasible. Record software versions and deterministic settings; PyTorch cautions that reproducibility is platform/version dependent ([documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html)).

Retain each user’s binary hit and compare paired differences. Adapt [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/) by resampling users within each category, preserving model pairing, then averaging the four category deltas; report a 95% interval and category results. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points within a category, or 0.125 macro points. Intervals remain conditional on seed=42 and the fixed candidate sets: they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability. Describe results explicitly as sampled HR@10; sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog rankings ([Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651)).

Predeclare evaluation cadence, checkpoint selection, tie-breaking and trial allocation. Record every attempted configuration and checkpoint comparison: repeated validation selection creates optimism, and an ordinary paired interval does not correct it ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Keep hidden test evaluation untouched. Under the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, report cumulative search cost including failures and diagnostics, alongside per-trial GPU-seconds, updates, epochs, nonpadding prediction targets, sampled negatives and selected checkpoint. Use matched training exposure for controlled ablations and matched compute for budget efficiency; equal runtime need not mean equal exposure.
